title: Essential Python libraries and their creators

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?

Libraries let a project reuse tested functionality. Python's standard-library asyncio module came from Guido van Rossum's PEP 3156 work and coordinates I/O waits. External projects include Travis Oliphant's NumPy for arrays, pandas (begun by Wes McKinney at AQR) for tables, John D. Hunter's Matplotlib for plots, Michael Waskom's Seaborn for statistical graphics, Samuel Colvin's Pydantic for validation, Michael Bayer's SQLAlchemy for SQL/ORM, Adrian Holovaty and Simon Willison's Django for newsroom web apps, and Sebastián Ramírez's FastAPI for typed HTTP APIs. Install external packages in a virtual environment and pin their versions.
CORE EXPLANATION

Start with Python's standard library: pathlib handles paths, json data exchange, csv table files, sqlite3 local databases, math and statistics calculations, and asyncio I/O-heavy waiting. The standard library is maintained by Python contributors, not one inventor. Install third-party packages inside a virtual environment. NumPy supports array computing, pandas tabular data, FastAPI HTTP APIs, and Django larger web applications. Travis Oliphant and the open-source community helped create NumPy; Adrian Holovaty and Simon Willison began Django to support newsroom work; Sebastián Ramírez created FastAPI. Before choosing a package, check its license, security updates, and supported Python versions.

from pathlib import Path

record = {"name": "Ada", "score": 10}
text = json.dumps(record)
Path("student.json").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
print(text)

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Start with the standard library; for the examples, run `python -m pip install numpy fastapi` in the active `.venv` and record dependencies.

spans.title: Important detail
spans.text: The standard library ships with Python. External packages such as NumPy, pandas, Django, and FastAPI must be installed and tracked as project dependencies.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Install packages in the project's .venv, keep secrets out of source code, and review third-party package provenance.
